newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Telstra says mobile phones demand boost sales.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Telstra says mobile phones demand boost sales.

text.p: Australia's state-owned telecommunications group Telstra Corp said on Friday strong demand for mobile phone services helped boost revenues in the 1995/96 year, but competition will pressure future sales growth.

Telstra earlier reported a 31.5 percent rise in net profit to A$2.30 billion for the year to June 30, 1996. Sales rose 8.1 percent to A$14.72 billion during the year, while expenses grew by eight percent to A$12.00 billion.
"The growth in revenues for the year as a whole reflected higher demand for telecommunications services, particularly in the mobiles, data, and ISDN businesses," Telstra said.

Telstra said the sales growth was achieved in spite of significant and increasing competition. Telstra held a monopoly on the local phone call market until the end of June, when Optus Vision started local telephony services.
Telstra faces competition in the long-distance and mobile phones markets. Australia's telecommunications market will be fully deregulated on July 1, 1997.

"Revenues in a number of key areas will continue to be subject to considerable pressures, as competition increases," Telstra said. It said it had also turned around the recent trend in which its costs grew faster than revenue.
Telstra said the rise in expenses was due to higher interconnect payments to other carriers, a rise in labour costs and higher directory publishing costs due to paper price rises.

"The results were achieved within the context of dynamic industry growth, increased pressure on Telstra's market share and competitiveness, and uncertainty about the future regulatory regime for telecommunications sector," Telstra's chief executive officer Frank Blount said in a statement.
"Despite these circumstances, margins have been held. Even more importantly, the corporation turned around the recent trend in which our costs grew faster than revenue," Blount said.

Telstra said capital expenditure grew by 22.1 percent to a record A$4.09 billion in 1995/96, which mainly reflected the rollout of its broadband network and expansion of its digital mobile phone network.

It said the rollout of its broadband network continued on schedule, and by the end of the year 1.2 million homes had access to the network, which carries the Telstra/News Corp Ltd jointly owned Foxtel pay television service.
"This strategic investment is meeting its current targets, and over the longer term will protect telephony revenues, and enhance Telstra's revenue streams and profitability," it said.
